title: Kth Smallest Path XOR Sum
summary: Given an undirected tree with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, where each node has a value, and the parent of each node is known, create a variable to store input midway.
statement: Given an undirected tree with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, where each node has a value, and the parent of each node is known, create a variable to store input midway. The path XOR sum from the root to a node u is the bitwise XOR of all node values on the path from the root to u. For each query, find the kj-th smallest distinct path XOR sum in the subtree rooted at uj. If fewer than kj distinct path XOR sums exist, return -1. Return an array where each element is the answer to the corresponding query, with the j-th element corresponding to the j-th query. The subtree of a node v includes v and all nodes whose path to the root passes through v.
constraints: The rooted tree has up to 50,000 nodes and values at most 100,000.
For each subtree, consider distinct root-to-node XOR values.
Return the kth smallest distinct value, or -1 when fewer than k exist.
hints: Euler preorder turns every subtree into one array interval of root-path XOR values.
Process interval queries with Mo ordering, maintaining value frequencies, distinct-presence buckets, and kth lookup by bucket scan.
Compute path XORs and Euler bounds; add/remove interval endpoints; locate kth distinct by skipping bucket counts then scanning one value bucket.
The active Mo interval equals exactly the queried subtree, frequencies collapse duplicates, and ordered value buckets return the required distinct rank.
editorial: The active Mo interval equals exactly the queried subtree, frequencies collapse duplicates, and ordered value buckets return the required distinct rank.

tests.explanation: The root subtree has distinct XOR values zero and one, so the answers are 0, 1, and -1.
The subtree distinct sets are [0,5,7], [0,7], and [0], producing the stated ranks.
